bullets: Diversification functions as a free lunch for individual investors by eliminating the risk of a single position going to zero — a critical buffer against behavioral risk during market stress.
Concentration with deep understanding creates a more robust portfolio than broad diversification, because it enables visibility into how positions interact and move together.
Diversification across a hundred names often reflects ignorance rather than safety, as it spreads ignorance evenly rather than managing risk through insight.
The real risk for individual investors is not concentration itself but the inability to withstand a loss — a behavioral challenge that diversification helps mitigate.
A concentrated portfolio can compound an investor's edge only if that edge survives the test of personal behavior — otherwise, no diversification will save them.
Account data shows that concentrated retail portfolios exhibit fatter tails — meaning higher risk of extreme losses — compared to diversified ones.
The key question isn't whether to diversify, but whether an investor's edge can endure their own emotional response to volatility.
A system of correlated bets works better when built on a few well-understood positions than on a hundred unfamiliar ones — understanding drives resilience.
